source: 外研社(新标准)选择性必修第二册 Unit 4 同主题阅读(无国界医生组织/一位医生的日记/全球村/林肯演说/埃德加·斯诺/银幕上的多元)。词限本单元/初中/常见词,答案转述非照抄,4选项唯一,与完形/听力关不撞。

passages.title: Doctors Without Borders
passages.body: Médecins Sans Frontières, known in English as Doctors Without Borders, was started in Paris in 1971 by a small group of doctors and journalists. From the very beginning, its idea was simple but powerful: medical help should cross every boundary. The organisation is independent and makes no profit. Its mission is to bring care to people who are affected by war, disease, natural disasters or a lack of basic health services. It helps people only according to their need, and it does not matter which country they come from. Those in the most serious and immediate danger are always treated first. Today the group has more than sixty thousand team members from over one hundred and fifty countries and regions. Doctors, nurses, drivers and local volunteers work side by side, often in places that other organisations have left. For them, a patient is never a foreigner. As one worker put it, there are no borders for doctors, for patients, or for anyone fighting a terrible disease.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: A group that brings medical care across all borders.
A factory that makes medicine for sale.
questions.explanation: 全文围绕'医疗援助跨越一切界限'的组织展开,是对其宗旨的概括。

questions.stem: Who receives treatment first, according to the text?
options: Those in the greatest and most urgent danger.
questions.explanation: 原文说处于最严重、最紧迫危险中的人优先受治,为转述。

questions.stem: How does the worker describe the group's view of patients?
options: No patient is treated as a foreigner.
Patients are judged by their wealth.
questions.explanation: 末句'对他们而言病人从不是外国人'的转述。

passages.title: A Doctor's Journal
passages.topic_cn: 记叙·一位医生的抗疫日记
passages.body: When I saw the tragic scenes on the news, I felt it was my duty as a doctor to go and offer help. I knew I was putting my life at risk, but I thought, if I don't do it, who will? So I joined the team fighting the outbreak. On my first day, a colleague spent an hour talking me through the daily routine. As she spoke, I could hear at least three different languages around us. My new comrades came from every continent except one. There was a young local man who carried the very sick into the clinic and worked hard to disinfect everything. There was a retired official whose team taught families how to prevent infection. Although the death rate was very high, we never gave up on a patient. One morning, against all odds, two infected brothers were still alive, and they later made a full recovery. That small success made up for many sadder cases. To share such work creates a powerful bond between people who have come from very different places.

questions.stem: Why did the writer decide to join the team?
options: He felt it was his duty to help.
He was ordered to go by the army.
He was looking for a holiday.
questions.explanation: 干扰项;正确答案见下条逻辑。原文'我觉得作为医生这是我的责任'。

questions.stem: What happened to the two infected brothers?
options: They both died the first night.
questions.explanation: 原文说兄弟俩奇迹般存活并完全康复,为转述。

questions.stem: What does the writer say such shared work creates?
options: A wish to give up the job.
Strong bonds between very different people.
questions.explanation: 末句'共同工作在不同背景的人之间建立起牢固纽带'的转述。

passages.title: The Global Village
passages.topic_cn: 说明·全球村与文化交流
passages.body: These days, people all over the world are becoming more and more connected, as if the planet were getting smaller and we were all living in one global village. Technology is largely responsible for bringing us together. Channels such as the mobile phone and the Internet have made it possible to speak instantly with someone on the other side of the world. This lets us form close ties with people of completely different cultures. Television, too, is like a window on the world, giving us quick and easy access to other ways of life. Cultural exchange helps us become more inclusive and to overcome culture shock. But being inclusive does not mean that our cultures will simply melt into one. Instead, it is about countries and people making a joint effort to come together and create a more harmonious world. In this way, everyone can enjoy the mutual benefits. The boundaries between cultures do not disappear; they just become bridges that we can cross.

questions.stem: What is mainly responsible for bringing people together?
questions.explanation: 原文'技术在很大程度上把人们联系到一起',为转述。

questions.stem: What does being inclusive NOT mean, according to the text?
options: All cultures melting into a single one.
questions.explanation: 原文说包容不意味着文化融为一体,为转述。

questions.stem: How are cultural boundaries described at the end?
options: As walls that must stay forever.
As bridges that can be crossed.
questions.explanation: 末句把界限比作'可以跨越的桥',为转述。

passages.title: The Words That Changed a Nation
passages.topic_cn: 记叙·林肯葛底斯堡演说
passages.body: On a grey afternoon in November 1863, a tall, thin man mounted a platform in a field in Gettysburg and began to speak. The place was the site of a recent battle where thousands of soldiers had died. The man was Abraham Lincoln, and he had come to honour those who had given their lives. His speech was only about two hundred and seventy words long and lasted just two minutes, yet it changed the minds of his people and helped shape a nation. At that time the country was bitterly divided by a civil war between the slave-owning South and the free North. The cost had been terrible, and many people had lost hope. Lincoln understood the feelings of ordinary civilians. His words gave them belief and a reason to look to the future. He offered a new vision of what the nation should be, one built on equality. Now, he said, it was up to the living to remove not only the divisions between North and South, but the boundaries between black and white.

questions.stem: What was special about Lincoln's speech?
options: It was about ten thousand words.
It was short but changed the nation.
questions.explanation: 原文强调演说短小却改变了国家,为转述。

questions.stem: Why had many people lost hope at that time?
options: Because of a costly civil war.
Because of a lack of schools.
questions.explanation: 原文说内战使国家分裂、代价惨重、人们失去希望,为转述。

questions.stem: What did Lincoln say the living should now do?
options: Remove the divisions and boundaries among people.
questions.explanation: 末句'消除南北分裂与黑白界限'的转述。

passages.title: An American Friend
passages.topic_cn: 说明·埃德加·斯诺打破隔阂
passages.body: Edgar Snow was an American journalist who wrote influential books and articles about China in the 1930s. At a time when very little was known about the country in the Western world, his 1937 book Red Star Over China broke down the boundaries of misunderstanding. It told the stories of the Chinese communist movement from the inside, and it did so in a way few outsiders ever managed. Snow was not the only foreign reporter to visit China in those years, but what set him apart was that he actually spent time with the Chinese Red Army. He listened to ordinary soldiers, watched their daily lives and talked with their leaders. His honest accounts of events such as the Long March captured the spirit of the people living through them. Because of this, Snow has long been called "our American friend". He risked his own safety to reach the heart of the story and to correct prejudice, building a bridge of understanding between two very different worlds.

questions.stem: What did Snow's 1937 book mainly do?
options: It taught people how to farm.
It sold maps of Western cities.
It broke down boundaries of misunderstanding about China.
It hid the truth about China.
questions.explanation: 原文说该书打破了西方对中国的隔阂,为转述。

questions.stem: What set Snow apart from other foreign reporters?
options: He could not speak any English.
He spent real time with the Red Army.
questions.explanation: 原文'让他与众不同的是他真正与红军相处',为转述。

questions.stem: Why is Snow remembered as "our American friend"?
options: Because he built understanding between two worlds.
Because he was born in China.
Because he never took any risks.
questions.explanation: 末段说他冒险纠正偏见、在两个世界间架起理解之桥,为转述。

passages.title: Breaking Boundaries on Screen
passages.topic_cn: 说明·银幕上的多元进步
passages.body: A recent report on diversity in Hollywood studied two hundred films and more than one thousand television shows. It found some good news: getting roles in American film and television is no longer quite so difficult for women and minority actors. Becoming a leading actor is now a more realistic hope for performers from minority backgrounds, and women are writing and directing films more often than before. This is a small but important advance against unfair treatment based on gender or race. Yet the report also showed that there is still a long way to go. Leading roles are more likely to be given to white actors, and Asian American performers in particular still face many problems. Even now, some studios cast white actors as Asian characters, which many people find unacceptable. Still, the overall message is hopeful. Step by step, the screen is becoming a place where more kinds of people can see themselves, and where old boundaries are slowly being pushed back.

questions.stem: What good news did the report find?
options: Acting roles have become easier to get for many performers.
Films are no longer made in America.
questions.explanation: 原文说女性和少数族裔获得角色不再那么难,为转述。

questions.stem: Which group still faces many problems, according to the text?
questions.explanation: 原文特别提到亚裔美国演员仍面临许多问题,为转述。

questions.stem: What is the overall message of the report?
options: Films should no longer be made.
questions.explanation: 末段说尽管仍有差距,整体是充满希望、界限正被慢慢推开,为转述。
